title: R’ Nachum, R’ Abbahu’s attendant
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Yevamot 42b, R’ Abbahu went along leaning on the shoulder of R’ Nachum, his attendant; he went along eliciting halakhah from him. He asked him, ‘A dispute followed by an anonymous teaching—what is the ruling?’ etc.
Hyman says it is possible that he is R’ Nachum mentioned in Berakhot, chapter 4, halakhah 3: R’ Zeira sent to R’ Nachum regarding R’ Yannai son of R’ Yishmael, etc.

In Berakhot, chapter 9, halakhah 2, and Taanit, chapter 1, halakhah 3, R’ Nachum, R’ Chizkiyah and R’ Ada bar Bimi (Taanit reads bar Ivuma) were sitting. R’ Nachum (Hyman says Berakhot mistakenly reads R’ Tanchum) said to R’ Abba bar Avimi, ‘Does it not make sense to recite the blessing?’ etc.
And in Beitzah, chapter 1, halakhah [supplied ה״מ; digital comparison 1:9]: Rabbi Nachum said in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Abba.
And in Bava Batra, beginning of chapter 4: Nachum in the name of R’ Chiya bar Abba.

notes.text: Shammaya describes Nachum’s role as attendant. The abbreviated Beitzah halakhah ה״מ remains irregular. Bimi/Ivuma and Nachum/Tanchum are Hyman’s reported variants and preferred readings.

The heading and other unsupported personal titles stay R-prime, including the father-title in Yannai son of R-prime Yishmael; the final bare Nachum remains untitled. The whole saved Guggenheimer Beitzah chapter 1 scalar [8][2] explicitly has רבי נחום אמר רבי שמואל בר אבא בעי, supporting full Rabbi only for the two names at this exact occurrence and a digital 1:9 comparison. Supplied ה״מ remains literal and unresolved; the match does not prove a mem/tet print error. Hyman’s compressed quotation is not expanded with the primary’s asked or its legal subject. Shammaya is an attendant role, not a new personal name. Yevamot’s he/from-him pronoun attachment is left unresolved; no new whole Yevamot check is claimed. Hyman’s possible cross-entry identity and Berakhot Tanchum error claim remain attributed, with Bimi/Ivuma and Abba bar Avimi distinct. The blessing question retains its negation and question form. Beginning Bava Batra chapter 4 is not its end or chapter 1. No printed or correction-history proof and no hold clearance are claimed.

The consulted Yevamot 42b–43a passage continues the exchange after Abbahu leans on his attendant. Rashi explains mankit as gathering settled rulings. The compressed wording here leaves the actor of the subsequent clause unstated. Jerusalem Berakhot 4:3 has Zeira send to Nachum concerning Yannai son of Yishmael. At 9:2 the consulted text has bracketed Nachum and Rav Ada bar Avimi, while Jerusalem Taanit 1:3 has Ada bar Ikhuma. These are textual comparisons beside Hyman’s Bimi, Ivuma and Tanchum readings. Jerusalem Beitzah 1:9 supplies Shmuel bar Abba’s question after Nachum’s report. The Hyman scan (vol. III, p. 922) appears to give ה״ט where the supplied text gives ה״מ. Jerusalem Bava Batra 4:1 names Rabbi Nachum in the name of Rabbi Chiyya bar Ba.
